lines.text: SVmma fuit ueterum regũq́; ducumq́; uoluptas,
lines.en: The greatest pleasure of ancient kings and leaders was,

lines.text: Illuſtris Princeps atauis, Erneſte Georgi,
lines.en: illustrious Prince from ancestors, Ernest George,

lines.text: Et motus cœli, cognataq́; ſidera ſummis
lines.en: both the motions of heaven, and the stars related to the highest

lines.text: Scrutari Diuis, & fata regentia mundum.
lines.en: Gods to examine, and the fates ruling the world.

lines.text: Scilicet ingentes animi, ſublimia corda,
lines.en: Namely, great minds, sublime hearts,

lines.text: Ætheream lucem (mortalia fœda peroſi)
lines.en: the ethereal light (hating foul mortal things)

lines.text: Quærebant, patrij luſtrantes limina templi.
lines.en: they sought, surveying the thresholds of the paternal temple.

lines.text: Turpe erat, errantum tanq̃ de more ferarum,
lines.en: It was shameful, as if in the manner of wandering beasts,

lines.text: Semiſepulta putri, defoſſaq́; lumina cœno
lines.en: half-buried in rotten, and dug-in eyes in mud

lines.text: In turpi fixiſſe ſolo: Sed tollere ſurſum,
lines.en: to have fixed in the foul soil: But to raise upwards,

lines.text: Fulgentesq́; notare oculis ſtellasq́; domusq́;
lines.en: and to note with eyes the shining stars and houses,

lines.text: Hoc opus, hic labor unus erat. Sic cognita tandem,
lines.en: This was the work, this was the one labor. Thus known at last,

lines.text: Ac ſubiecta homini ſunt conſcia ſidera fati,
lines.en: And subjected to man are the stars conscious of fate,

lines.text: Et quæcunq́; uagi ſpacioſa uolumina mundi
lines.en: And whatever spacious volumes of the wandering world

lines.text: Obſcuris habuere prius demerſa latebris.
lines.en: they had previously submerged in obscure hiding places.

lines.text: Hinc Lybicus memoratur Atlas, quẽ prodidit axem,
lines.en: Hence Libyan Atlas is remembered, who brought forth the axis,

lines.text: Suſtinuiſſe micantem humeris, ſtellisq́; coruſcum,
lines.en: to have sustained the shining one on his shoulders, and flashing with stars,

lines.text: Heroum fingens uariè ingenioſa uetuſtas,
lines.en: ingenious antiquity variously fashioning of heroes,

lines.text: Et quaſi picta ſua referens decora inclyta laude.
lines.en: And as if painted, bringing back its renowned honors with praise.

lines.text: Sic tuus, O tellus Bœotica fortis Orion
lines.en: Thus your strong Orion, O Boeotian land,

lines.text: Dicitur aſſiduo ſtudio comes iſſe Dianæ,
lines.en: Is said to have gone as a companion of Diana with constant zeal,

sections.text:
AD ILLVSTREM
AC GENEROSVM PRINCI-
PEM AC DOMINVM D. GEORGIVM
Erneſtum Comitem Hennenbergenſem, Nuncupa-
torium Carmen Ioachimi Helleri Leucopetræi.
sections.en:
TO THE ILLUSTRIOUS
AND NOBLE PRINCE
AND LORD, LORD GEORGE
Ernest, Count of Henneberg, Dedicatory
Poem of Joachim Heller of Weißenfels.

summary.headline: Heller’s Dedicatory Poem
summary.text: Opening of Joachim Heller’s dedicatory poem to George Ernest, Count of Henneberg, praising ancient rulers who studied the motions of heaven, stars, celestial houses, and fate. The poem invokes Atlas and Orion as mythic exemplars of stellar knowledge.
